I added a 0.25s sleep after each sandbox call in `tests/test_payments.py`. I didn't run the test, since it calls the real sandbox.

- **Delay:** 5 requests per second means at least 0.2s between calls. I used 0.25s to leave some room for timing jitter. The value is in a named constant, `SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL`, with a comment explaining the rate limit.
- **Placement:** The sleep comes after the assert, so a failed request stops the test straight away instead of waiting first.
- **Cost:** The test takes about 1 second longer for its 4 calls.

If other tests in the same CI run also call the sandbox at the same time, this won't stop them from going over the limit together. A shared rate limiter or retrying on 429 responses would handle that, if it turns out to be a problem.

I also saved the 5 requests-per-second limit to my memory for this project, so any new sandbox tests will get the same pacing.
